text: Published agreement: Financing Agreement for IDA Credit 7075-UG and Grant D9970-UG (signed 20 February 2023). Latest restructuring paper: RES02060 (18 August 2026), the project's third restructuring.

Agreement - effectiveness conditions (Article V, Section 5.01, pp. 3-4): the Bank satisfied that Uganda has an adequate refugee protection framework; MEMD has set up the Project Coordination Unit with a coordination manager, project accountant and environmental and social safeguards specialists; MEMD has set up its PIU (grid expansion manager, senior legal officer, project manager, connections manager, safeguards and procurement specialists, etc.); 90-day effectiveness deadline (Section 5.02). Further staffing within six months of effectiveness: 9 more PCU staff, 18 more MEMD-PIU staff and 9 more UECCC-PIU staff, with key positions retained (Schedule 2).

Agreement - performance-based conditions (Schedule 4, pp. 30-31): PBC 1, MEMD analyses a proposal for optimized grid design and connection materials with the Electricity Regulatory Authority and decides on the study findings within two years of implementation (SDR 358,750); PBC 2, MEMD's E&S capacity and tools, health, safety and GBV training, a working grievance mechanism and timely compensation of project-affected persons, assessed each fiscal year (SDR 286,850 a year, SDR 1,434,250 in total); PBC 3, UECCC runs nationwide energy market consultations and reports findings (SDR 143,425 a year); PBC 4, operation and maintenance costs for public institutions' solar systems paid in full and on time to service providers (SDR 3,585,875). The Government must budget these O&M costs in its MTEF: US$0 in FY1, US$500,000 in FY2, US$1.5 million in FY3, US$2 million in FY4 and US$1 million in FY5 (Section IV.A, p. 28). Closing date 30 June 2027 (p. 28).

Latest restructuring paper (pp. 1, 4-5): reallocates US$20 million (SDR 14,634,218) of the IDA grant - US$10 million from Component 1 (grid) to sub-component 2.1 and US$10 million from the refugee-window grid sub-component 3.1 to 3.2 (financial intermediation) - because RBF grid connections are slow and fewer ready boards are being bought; revises PDO targets, e.g. connections from 1,571,500 to 1,600,200, people with grid access from 5,050,000 to 4,800,000, people in refugee-hosting districts from 534,000 to 928,000, clean cooking from 1,660,000 to 1,900,000; the RBF operations manual is updated with tighter ESCO eligibility, claims verification and anti-fraud controls. No change to the PDO, closing date, components or legal covenants. It recalls the earlier restructurings: October 2025 (US$10 million to Component 2) and June 2026 (CTF grant closing extended to 30 June 2027).

Questions to raise with the ministry: How will MEMD and UEDCL reach the grid targets after Umeme's exit, and when will connection materials arrive? What did the PBC 1 grid-design study conclude, and was the decision taken within the two-year window? Are the O&M budget allocations for public-institution solar systems in the MTEF as the agreement requires (PBC 4)? With closing in June 2027 and the grant 34% disbursed in the latest ISR, is an extension being considered? How will the new anti-fraud and verification controls in the RBF schemes be enforced? These are suggestions derived from the documents, not issues the documents themselves raise.
